notes: kb/Work PB5070 owns the mechanism (PADDING CHARACTER is a grammar rule no binder reads); it lists the clause's syntax rules 1 and 3, not this format row or the subscripted operand. §1985:VII.2.7.2 prints PADDING CHARACTER IS { data-name-1 | literal-1 }, PADDING the one underlined word. Implemented at 85: paddingCharacterClause is PADDING CHARACTER? IS? (literal | dataReference), an alternative of fileControlClauses, so the clause parses with either optional word omitted and with a literal or a (qualified) data-name; ScreenClauseRepetition refuses a second clause (COBOL2423); VisitPaddingCharacterClause leaves it alone at 85, warns at 2002 (COBOL0903) and refuses it from 2014 (COBOL0902). Probed at 85: PADDING CHARACTER IS "*", PADDING IS, PADDING CHARACTER and a bare PADDING before the literal, a data-name and PC1 OF G1 compile and run; no operand, two operands, PADDING CHARACTERS ARE, and CHARACTER IS without PADDING are refused. Not implemented: the operand class data-name-1. The grammar takes a full dataReference and BindFileControl has no arm for the clause, so nothing resolves or screens the operand: a subscripted name (PC1 (1)), a reference-modified name (WS1 (1:1)) and a name defined nowhere all compile clean at 85. §1985:III.2 defines the format's word: 'data-name' represents a word which must not be reference-modified, subscripted, or qualified unless specifically permitted by the rules of the format, and §1985:VII.2.7.3 SR2 permits qualification only. The clause is inert in the object program (no blocking model), so the harm is acceptance of non-conforming source, not a wrong result. The witness writes PADDING CHARACTER IS "*" on a sequential file and reads one record back.

next.reason: §1985:VII.2.7.2 is the clause 'PADDING CHARACTER IS {data-name-1 | literal-1}' of a sequential file control entry. 2023 has no PADDING CHARACTER clause: the clauses of the file control entry, §2023:12.4.5.1 'Format 3 (sequential)', are ASSIGN, ACCESS MODE, FILE STATUS, LOCK MODE, ORGANIZATION, RECORD DELIMITER, RESERVE and SHARING, and the words occur in 2023 only in the prose of §2023:9.1.1 ('Padding characters are added or deleted as necessary'), which states no clause. A 1985 entry with PADDING CHARACTER is refused by a 2023 compiler: REMOVED.
